Samantha Hudspeth

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Samantha Hudspeth was shot through her face and neck by her abusive boyfriend and left for dead. A series of heroic acts ensued and gave her a new lease on life.

Unique Selling Point:
Every day three women die at the hands of their intimate partner in South Africa (July 2018 – South African Human Rights Commission). This too could have been the fate of Samantha Hudspeth, when her boyfriend of two years shot her early in the morning of the 19th of April, in traffic while she was driving. He had stalked her, walked up to her car and shot her through the face and neck and left her for dead. She was driving to finish off her statement of assault and abuse at the Douglasdale police station, which she had laid the night before, after he attacked her and her friend in their apartment. Quick response by Fourways Life paramedics, and life saving surgery has given her the opportunity to start over. Although still in recovery, she is back at work as she has no other means of surviving. She is a hope of glimmer for women who have been through similar ordeals and need to find a way to pick up their lives and start again.

Summary:
Samantha was shot by her former fiancé Mitchell Osborne in broad daylight outside the entrance to Fourways life hospital in Sandton on the morning of 19 April 2019. He sped away from the scene and shot himself dead shortly afterwards when apprehended by the SAP.
She was saved by by the Fourways Life Paramedics who took 6 minutes to get her out of her car and into the emergency, where later she was operated on by Dr Mati, a brilliant surgeon who saved her life. She was shot with hollow point bullets and one was still lodged just millimeters from her spine.
Once she started recovery, she was left homeless and without work, as her boyfriend was so controlling he had made her give up her job. She moved in with her 26 year old son and barely out of surgery started looking for work as a car sales person. Mercedes who she had worked for before, knew of her ordeal and gave her a job, knowing that it will take her some time to recover fully.

Carte Blanche tells the story of the amazing acts of heroism and kindness that saved Samantha’s life as well as helped her get back on her feat. We also confront the state and the police as to why no action was taken to apprehend Mitchell Osbourne the night before when he threatened to kill her because she was leaving.

Further information:
Mitchell was a well to do member of the Sandton scene and co-director of Performance Plant hire with his twin brother. Mitchell had a history of abusive and violent behaviour, some of which we will be able to document. He had a tumultuous relationship with Samantha and she was in the process of exiting the relationship, with the assistance of their shared psychologist, when the incident occurred. She grew tired of his controlling abusive ways and moved out of his house. In fact, the last time she saw him before the incident was the Monday night before she was shot when she went to his house to fetch a hairdryer and some clothes. Once again he acted abusively, threatened to kill her and assaulted her friend Courtney by punching her in the face - a shocking scene for the community of people in the gated complex. She and Courtney went to the SAPS at Douglasdale immediately thereafter where they laid a charge against Mitchell. They notified the police that he had threatened to kill them, possessed guns and that they feared for their lives. They asked the SAPS to confiscate the weapons. The SAPS response was lack lustre and one even stated that it was not worth the bother of even taking statements because they would simply withdraw the charges by tomorrow! No one bothered to go and investigate or confiscate the weapons. They called Mitchell but he did not answer and opined they would not get into the complex because of the security. Samantha and Courtney protested stoutly and as a result Courtney’s statement was eventually taken and they made arrangements to go back the next morning to minute Samantha’s statement because it was late and Courtney was anxious to get home to her child who was home alone.
The following morning as Samantha was on her way to the SAPS Mitchell appeared and shot her twice, while she was in her car and stationary in traffic, once in the neck and then once in the face through her left cheek. She did not see Mitchell coming. He shot her with hollow-point bullets for maximum destructive impact and casually left her for dead. The incident was witnessed by a number of people including Nicola Capstickdale, who is still deeply traumatised by what she saw.
Samantha should have died and indeed that would have been the case had he not shot her outside a hospital. Incredibly two advanced life support paramedics, Riaan and Matthew, were in the parking lot of the hospital and witnessed the shooting. They immediately went to her assistance, stabilising her condition and getting her into critical care within a few minutes where the doctors of Fourways Life worked furiously to engineer a miracle. She suffered very severe injuries and will have to have multiple surgeries to repair the damage but survived. Amazingly she is already out of hospital and back at work putting her life back together. She has been offered employment by Mercedes who have decided to support her through what is anticipated to be a long recovery.
The community has rallied around her in support and numerous prayer groups were set up to help Samantha to pull her through the traumatic ordeal. Her story is one of triumph and hope.

Press Release:


One fateful night a woman begs the police to take away her ex-fiance’s guns. The next morning she’s fighting for her life. Shot in broad daylight and left for dead by her abusive ex-fiance, Samantha Wade is forever grateful to the medical heroes who miraculously saved her life.

Script:


LINK: It was on this busy street just after 7 in the morning in Fourways Johannesburg on the 19th of March this year when Samantha Wade's ex fiance walked up to her car and shot her twice, leaving her for dead.

Samantha: (NI): I knew it wasn’t a hijacking… I just, I just felt it… and I felt that it was him…

VO: CCTV footage from the surrounds captured the movements of his Range Rover that morning, and reveals a disturbing sequence of events.

Samantha [NI]: He waited for me down the road, saw me leave and chased after me… I didn't see him behind me he had half an hour sitting there to change his mind… that's what haunts me...

VO: Cameras at the nearby Life Hospital Fourways witness the moment when he gets out of his Range Rover… then we lose sight of him, which is when he shoots her through the window, seconds later he returns to his car

Matthew: We heard a loud bang. I said to Riaan it sounded like a gunshot - we looked around to see where the sound was coming from. I saw a white car reverse suddenly and speed off.

VO: Advanced Life Support paramedics Matthew Bostwick and Riaan Nothnagel were first to respond.

Riaan: I got next to the vehicle, saw the two holes through the window

Samantha: I just remember hearing this voice saying unlock the door, I was pressing my finger on the unlock button and it just wouldn’t unlock and eventually I pressed with everything that I had and it unlocked and then I don't remember anything.

Riaan: The door opened and that’s when we saw what happened

Matthew: massive facial trauma, lots of bleeding

Riaan: two wounds, one in the neck, one in the cheek. So we applied direct pressure to both of the wounds to stop the bleeding at that point in time

Matthew: And we cleared a lot of blood from the airway which was swollen, but our main focus was of course getting her into a safe and secure environment.

VO: Samantha felt increasingly unsafe in the preceding weeks, as her ex-fiance's violent outbursts reached tipping point, that fateful morning

LINK: After a witness alerted the police, they spotted his vehicle on Witkoppen road but before they could apprehend him, he shot and killed himself.

Samantha: I can't come to terms that this was not fixable… and now he's gone and left a trail of destruction.

VO: He was a businessman in his 50's from the North of Johannesburg, whose name will not be mentioned, out of respect for Samantha's wishes.

Samantha: Socially he was very popular, he was loving, he was caring, but once I entered into an intimate relationship with him the signs of emotional and verbal abuse became evident

VO: Samantha believed she knew him well before their two year relationship began. They had known each other throughout their previous marriages and were family friends for 35 years.

Masa: How did this aggression and red flags manifest?

Samantha: When he started feeling that he lost control of me his anger would then appear, he would constantly check up on me.

VO: He also told Samantha her friends were no longer welcome, and asked her to give up her job so they could spend more time together.

Samantha: He just wanted my attention 24/7

VO: Unable to cope with his behaviour Samantha eventually moved out of his house.

Masa: Why didn’t you leave sooner?

Samantha: He would promise he would never do it again, he would promise he would change

VO: They continued to work on their relationship with a therapist, who advised Samantha to move back in to the home. Even though Samantha felt insecure and afraid, she decided to give it one more try, a mere week before the shooting.

Samantha: As soon as I moved back in, it took him one day to revert back to this control …. he screamed he shouted...and he became aggressive with me. Eventually I locked myself in the spare room. He would whatsapp me that he would never hurt me, he loved me too much.

VO: A few days later, he hunted her down.

Samantha: The one bullet went in here, and shattered everything in my mouth. The next bullet went through my neck and ended up i think a millimeter away from my spine

LINK: It took 6 minutes after the shooting for the paramedics to get Samantha Wade into these emergency rooms at the Life Fourways Hospital

Doctor Kozaczynski: Our doctor from casualty was able to perform the similar procedure to the tracheostomy and preventing blood coming to the lungs. If this not happen she will be dead.

VO: Dr Karol Kozaczynski, a Specialist Surgeon, performed more life saving surgery, removing the bullet close to her spine.

Masa: What kind of injuries did she sustain?

Doctor Kozaczynski: Several shot in her face but fortunately below the brain. From the nose down there was nothing, its pieces all of the small fragments of bones which you cannot even put together.

VO: Samantha was shot with hollow point bullets that expand on impact - this MRI scan shows the extent of her injuries.

Dr Nokaneng: Everything in her face was damaged.


VO: Dr Emmy Nokaneng, a maxillo-facial and oral surgeon, was responsible for reconstructing Samantha's face.

Dr Nokaneng:We had to struggle with a tooth that was lodged inside her lung, so after 2, 3 hours we managed to remove that tooth.

VO: What followed was eight hours of surgery.

Dr Nokaneng: So I started with the lower jaw on the left hand side that was shattered into three pieces, I had to put in a titanium plate to secure those pieces together. And in the upper jaw in the palate was a big hole there where you could see right through to the base of the skull.

VO: A major complication was Samantha's tongue which had been sliced laterally and had to be re-attached.

Masa: Did you at any point think he would actually shoot you?

Samantha: The week before, it crossed my mind.

VO: During that last harrowing week, Samantha decided to move out again, and went back to fetch some clothes with a friend.

Samantha: He was completely drunk.

VO: He became aggressive and her friend tried to protect her.

Samantha: The next thing he hit her in the face and she fell to the ground.

VO: He locked them in the bedroom, and threatened to shoot them, but they managed to escape..

LINK: Samantha and her friend came to the Douglasdale police station to lay charges of assault and intimidation against her ex fiance, asking the police to either arrest him or confiscate his firearms as they feared for their lives.

Samantha: The commander of the police station said this is a domestic dispute by tomorrow it will be over, and we were begging him please go there and confiscate the guns.

VO: Before going to the police station, Samantha's friend, had made contact with Advocate Jean Berdou from the Douglasdale Community Policing Forum.

Jean: I was informed that one of the ladies had been injured and I arranged for a paramedic to assess the lady, she was fine, and I was assured by the commander the matter would receive the requisite attention. Well the next morning the shooting occurred and it became very clear there was a big problem

Masa: What should the police have done?

Jean: My understanding of the domestic violence protection act is that if there's an allegation of a firearm involved, that should have been investigated and the steps taken to secure the presence of that firearm.

VO: In a bitter twist of fate, Samantha was heading back to the Douglasdale police station to complete her statement, when her ex-fiance gunned her down. //

Her attorney, Egg-on Oswald has sent a letter of demand to the Minister of Police, claiming negligence on the part of Douglasdale police and is suing for damages.

Egon: They should have firstly gone and apprehended him and they should have confiscated those firearms. If that had happened then her life would be completely different.

VO: South African Police Spokesperson for Gauteng, Brigadier Mathapelo Peters is unable to discuss specifics of the case as litigation is pending.//

In the meantime Samantha is still struggling to come to terms with what happened.

Samantha: I'm grateful to be alive, I am. But every day I wake up and I make a mental decision that I will be strong.

VO: Samantha's road to recovery will be a long one. But already, three months later, she's working and feels supported.

Samantha (NI): My children got me through this, and my will to live. Angels were with me, that's why I’m here today.

VO: He locked them in the bedroom, and threatened to shoot them, but they managed to escape.. LINK: Samantha and her friend came to the Douglasdale police station to lay charges of assault and intimidation against her ex fiance, asking the police to either arrest him or confiscate his firearms as they feared for their lives. Samantha: The commander of the police station said this is a domestic dispute by tomorrow it will be over, and we were begging him please go there and confiscate the guns. VO: Before going to the police station, Samantha's friend, had made contact with Advocate Jean Berdou from the Douglasdale Community Policing Forum. Jean: I was informed that one of the ladies had been injured and I arranged for a paramedic to assess the lady, she was fine, and I was assured by the commander the matter would receive the requisite attention. Well the next morning the shooting occurred and it became very clear there was a big problem Masa: What should the police have done? Jean: My understanding of the domestic violence protection act is that if there's an allegation of a firearm involved, that should have been investigated and the steps taken to secure the presence of that firearm. VO: In a bitter twist of fate, Samantha was heading back to the Douglasdale police station to complete her statement, when her ex-fiance gunned her down. // Her attorney, Egg-on Oswald has sent a letter of demand to the Minister of Police, claiming negligence on the part of Douglasdale police and is suing for damages. Egon: They should have firstly gone and apprehended him and they should have confiscated those firearms. If that had happened then her life would be completely different. VO: South African Police Spokesperson for Gauteng, Brigadier Mathapelo Peters is unable to discuss specifics of the case as litigation is pending.// In the meantime Samantha is still struggling to come to terms with what happened. Samantha: I'm grateful to be alive, I am. But every day I wake up and I make a mental decision that I will be strong. VO: Samantha's road to recovery will be a long one. But already, three months later, she's working and feels supported. Samantha (NI): My children got me through this, and my will to live. Angels were with me, that's why I’m here today.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Samantha Hudspeth was shot through her face and neck by her abusive boyfriend and left for dead. A series of heroic acts ensued and gave her a new lease on life.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Every day three women die at the hands of their intimate partner in South Africa (July 2018 – South African Human Rights Commission). This too could have been the fate of Samantha Hudspeth, when her boyfriend of two years shot her early in the morning of the 19th of April, in traffic while she was driving. He had stalked her, walked up to her car and shot her through the face and neck and left her for dead. She was driving to finish off her statement of assault and abuse at the Douglasdale police station, which she had laid the night before, after he attacked her and her friend in their apartment. Quick response by Fourways Life paramedics, and life saving surgery has given her the opportunity to start over. Although still in recovery, she is back at work as she has no other means of surviving. She is a hope of glimmer for women who have been through similar ordeals and need to find a way to pick up their lives and start again.
metadata.Summary: Samantha was shot by her former fiancé Mitchell Osborne in broad daylight outside the entrance to Fourways life hospital in Sandton on the morning of 19 April 2019. He sped away from the scene and shot himself dead shortly afterwards when apprehended by the SAP. She was saved by by the Fourways Life Paramedics who took 6 minutes to get her out of her car and into the emergency, where later she was operated on by Dr Mati, a brilliant surgeon who saved her life. She was shot with hollow point bullets and one was still lodged just millimeters from her spine. Once she started recovery, she was left homeless and without work, as her boyfriend was so controlling he had made her give up her job. She moved in with her 26 year old son and barely out of surgery started looking for work as a car sales person. Mercedes who she had worked for before, knew of her ordeal and gave her a job, knowing that it will take her some time to recover fully. Carte Blanche tells the story of the amazing acts of heroism and kindness that saved Samantha’s life as well as helped her get back on her feat. We also confront the state and the police as to why no action was taken to apprehend Mitchell Osbourne the night before when he threatened to kill her because she was leaving.
metadata.Further information: Mitchell was a well to do member of the Sandton scene and co-director of Performance Plant hire with his twin brother. Mitchell had a history of abusive and violent behaviour, some of which we will be able to document. He had a tumultuous relationship with Samantha and she was in the process of exiting the relationship, with the assistance of their shared psychologist, when the incident occurred. She grew tired of his controlling abusive ways and moved out of his house. In fact, the last time she saw him before the incident was the Monday night before she was shot when she went to his house to fetch a hairdryer and some clothes. Once again he acted abusively, threatened to kill her and assaulted her friend Courtney by punching her in the face - a shocking scene for the community of people in the gated complex. She and Courtney went to the SAPS at Douglasdale immediately thereafter where they laid a charge against Mitchell. They notified the police that he had threatened to kill them, possessed guns and that they feared for their lives. They asked the SAPS to confiscate the weapons. The SAPS response was lack lustre and one even stated that it was not worth the bother of even taking statements because they would simply withdraw the charges by tomorrow! No one bothered to go and investigate or confiscate the weapons. They called Mitchell but he did not answer and opined they would not get into the complex because of the security. Samantha and Courtney protested stoutly and as a result Courtney’s statement was eventually taken and they made arrangements to go back the next morning to minute Samantha’s statement because it was late and Courtney was anxious to get home to her child who was home alone. The following morning as Samantha was on her way to the SAPS Mitchell appeared and shot her twice, while she was in her car and stationary in traffic, once in the neck and then once in the face through her left cheek. She did not see Mitchell coming. He shot her with hollow-point bullets for maximum destructive impact and casually left her for dead. The incident was witnessed by a number of people including Nicola Capstickdale, who is still deeply traumatised by what she saw. Samantha should have died and indeed that would have been the case had he not shot her outside a hospital. Incredibly two advanced life support paramedics, Riaan and Matthew, were in the parking lot of the hospital and witnessed the shooting. They immediately went to her assistance, stabilising her condition and getting her into critical care within a few minutes where the doctors of Fourways Life worked furiously to engineer a miracle. She suffered very severe injuries and will have to have multiple surgeries to repair the damage but survived. Amazingly she is already out of hospital and back at work putting her life back together. She has been offered employment by Mercedes who have decided to support her through what is anticipated to be a long recovery. The community has rallied around her in support and numerous prayer groups were set up to help Samantha to pull her through the traumatic ordeal. Her story is one of triumph and hope.
